top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) recognises a mature, first-order empirical discovery: import exposure produced concentrated, slow and persistent local labour-market adjustment costs, overturning the prior that workers and regions reallocate quickly. The transparent local-labour-market designs have been replicated, challenged on shift-share identification and exposure measurement, and extended for over a decade. The sign and local concentration of the effects have survived in qualified form, while long-run magnitudes remain debated, so the citation should credit exposure and adjustment evidence and claim no effect size or ruling on the origin of the task framework. Attribution to the three jointly authoring names is the tightest on the slate. P002 (Helpman, Melitz) is mature with a clean mechanism, but its priority questions (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) and overlap with the 2008 prize are unresolved, and its welfare claims are structure-dependent. P000 is ranked last because at least two defensible awards exist.
recusal_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent from the profile. Disclosed ties: co-authorship with John Hassler (chair) and frequent co-authorship with Per Krusell (secretary), and IIES colleague of both. Long-running collaboration with Klenow (B010), which is not on the slate. Heterogeneous-firm and firm-dynamics work adjacent to B034 (P002), ranked second. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
